filings.headline: Maharashtra GST dept conducts Section 67 search at IG Petrochem premises
filings.summary: The Commissioner of State Tax, Maharashtra initiated an inspection/search under Section 67 of the Maharashtra GST Act, 2017 at the company's premises on 17 November 2026; the inspection was ongoing. The company says there is no communication yet on alleged violations and no impact on financials or operations. A tax search is treated as material regardless of amount, though no figure or demand has been disclosed.
filings.impactWhy: Tax search ongoing without quantified demand or material outcome

filings.headline: India Ratings upgrades Sobha to IND AA/Stable from IND AA-/Positive
filings.summary: India Ratings & Research upgraded Sobha's Issuer Rating and long-term bank loan facilities to IND AA/Stable from IND AA-/Positive, and affirmed short-term facilities at IND A1+. It also assigned IND AA/Stable to proposed NCDs. The upgrade signals improved credit profile and lower borrowing costs.
filings.impactWhy: Credit rating upgraded to IND AA from IND AA-

filings.headline: Preferential issue: 12.24L shares at ₹1,674.47 raising ₹205cr (AIFs)
filings.summary: Aimtron allotted 12,24,265 equity shares at ₹1,674.47 each (premium ₹1,664.47) to seven non-promoter AIFs, aggregating ₹204.99cr. This adds about 5.9% more shares (~5.6% dilution to existing holders on the ~2.08cr base), at an issue price slightly below the current ₹1,858.1. Clarus Capital 1 takes the largest stake at 3.15% post-issue; the raise is roughly a third of ₹629cr yearly sales.
filings.impactWhy: Preferential issue exceeding 5% dilution raising ₹205cr

filings.headline: Promoter group bought 1.5% (₹14.5cr) at about ₹610
filings.summary: Promoter Basant Kumar Kabra, promoter and director Shiva Basant Kabra, and promoter group entity Silver Plastochem Private Limited bought 2,37,777 shares (1.5% of the company) through market purchases for ₹14.5 crore. The shares were acquired at an average price of ₹610 compared to the current price of ₹585, raising their holding from 43.9% to 45.4%.
filings.impactWhy: Promoter group bought 1.5% stake for ₹14.5 crore.

filings.headline: Promoter group bought 0.08% (₹6.5cr) at about ₹136
filings.summary: Promoter entities Sirisha Projects Private Limited and A V S R Holdings Private Limited bought a 0.08% stake in NCC for ₹6.5 crore through market purchases at an average price of ₹136, compared to the current price of ₹134. This increased their holding from 15.1% to 15.2%.
filings.impactWhy: Promoter entities bought 0.08% stake in company.

filings.headline: Subsidiary's Mehsana plant gets PIC/S GMP nod from Ukraine regulator
filings.summary: Senores' subsidiary Ratnatris Pharmaceuticals' Mehsana, Gujarat facility received PIC/S GMP certification from Ukraine's SMDC, issued Nov 16, 2026. The approval gives the company an expanded regulatory pathway into semi-regulated markets. No financial figures were disclosed, but it widens the CDMO's addressable export markets.
filings.impactWhy: PIC/S GMP certification from Ukraine regulator; no financial impact disclosed.

filings.headline: Signs tech pact with Versalis for 2nd 70 KTPA mABS line; ₹450cr capex
filings.summary: Supreme Petrochem executed a Technology Agreement with Versalis S.p.A for a 2nd mABS line of 70 KTPA, to be mechanically completed by December 2028. Investment of ₹450 crore (about 6.8% of ₹6586cr yearly sales) will be funded via internal accruals, doubling mABS capacity from the existing 70 KTPA line (running at 60% utilization). Expansion targets growing ABS demand in India.
filings.impactWhy: Capex agreement for expansion completing in 2028, under 10% of sales.

filings.headline: Ashoka L1 for NHAI Vadodara-Mumbai Expressway pkg at ₹1,465cr
filings.summary: Ashoka Buildcon declared lowest bidder (L-1) for NHAI's 8-lane Vadodara-Mumbai Expressway balance work (Km 154.6-190, Pkg-VIII) in Gujarat on EPC mode, quoted EPC price ₹1,465cr excl. GST. The order is about 21.6% of last 12 months' sales of ₹6,786cr, so it is a significant addition to the order book. Execution period is 18 months with a 10-year defect liability period.
filings.impactWhy: L-1 for NHAI project worth ₹1,465cr, 21.6% of sales.

filings.headline: Advait wins ₹130.5cr GETCO reconductoring order, ~16% of sales
filings.summary: Advait Energy received an order from Gujarat Energy Transmission Corporation (GETCO) for supply, installation, testing and commissioning of reconductoring of the 220kV Dahej–Haldarwa Line-1 & Line-2, Bharuch Circle, with higher-ampacity conductor. The order is worth ₹130.49cr (incl taxes) and is to be executed over 15 months. That is about 15.6% of the ₹839cr last-12-months sales, a sizeable domestic win.
filings.impactWhy: Order win of ₹130.5cr represents 15.6% of annual sales.

filings.headline: Postal ballot to add new main objects in MoA, voting ends Dec 19
filings.summary: Route Mobile has issued a postal ballot notice seeking shareholder approval via special resolution to alter its Memorandum of Association by inserting new main object clauses (nos. 2, 3, 4 and 5) after existing clause 1. Remote e-voting runs from November 20 to December 19, 2026, with results by December 22, 2026. A change to the company's main business objects can signal expansion into new business lines, making it worth watching.
filings.impactWhy: Postal ballot for altering objects clause of Memorandum of Association.

filings.headline: Shareholders approve alteration of objects clause to add new business objects
filings.summary: Via postal ballot, shareholders passed a special resolution to alter the Memorandum's objects clause by substituting an existing main object and inserting new objects, approved with 99.67% votes in favour. Two independent directors (Prakash Kumar Behera and Kajal Mayur Saiya) were also appointed to fill casual vacancies. The change in business objects signals a potential expansion or shift in the company's activities.
filings.impactWhy: Shareholder approval for altering objects clause and independent director appointments.

filings.headline: Won 474.66 acres in Raigad MMR for ₹194.19cr via subsidiary consortium
filings.summary: Signatureglobal's wholly owned subsidiary Maa Vaishno Net-Tech Ltd led a consortium that won 474.66 acres in Raigad, Maharashtra (part of MMR) for ₹194.19cr, about 7% of yearly sales, marking a strategic entry into the Mumbai Metropolitan Region beyond its NCR base. Post approvals, 35% of the subsidiary's equity will be diluted to consortium partners, with Signatureglobal retaining 65%. The move opens a new geography near Navi Mumbai Airport, though product plans are still being evaluated.
filings.impactWhy: Land acquisition worth ~7% of sales; routine real estate land purchase.

filings.headline: CRISIL cuts outlook to Negative, reaffirms A+/A1 on Rs 2,099cr facilities
filings.summary: CRISIL revised ION Exchange's long-term outlook to 'Negative' from 'Stable' while reaffirming CRISIL A+/A1 on Rs 2,099.74 crore bank facilities. The cut reflects weak H1FY27 performance: revenue up just 4.5% to Rs 1,375cr but operating margin at negative 3.8% (vs 9.9% a year ago), driven by a ~Rs 90cr one-time provision on legacy EPC projects, higher raw material costs and slow Roha plant ramp-up. FY27 operating margin is seen at just 4-5%, signalling a material deterioration in profitability.
filings.impactWhy: Rating reaffirmed with outlook revision; not an upgrade or downgrade.

filings.headline: Material WOS GK Energy Solar adds green hydrogen, ammonia, storage to objects
filings.summary: RoC Pune approved altering the Main Object Clause of material wholly-owned subsidiary GK Energy Solar Private Limited, inserting new sub-clauses to enter green hydrogen, green ammonia, green methanol, e-fuels, electrolysers, fuel cells and battery/energy-storage businesses. The change was approved via special resolution to diversify into new green-energy lines. This signals a potential new business direction for the group, though no investment size or financials are disclosed.
filings.impactWhy: Alteration of subsidiary object clause without disclosed financial size.

filings.headline: US FDA classifies Caplin Steriles' Gummidipoondi plant as OAI
filings.summary: The US FDA classified Caplin Steriles' (subsidiary) injectable and ophthalmic facility at Gummidipoondi as 'Official Action Indicated' (OAI) following an August 13-21, 2026 inspection that ended with 10 procedural observations. The company says there is no material impact on financials or operations and the facility continues manufacturing and supply. An OAI is a regulatory red flag that can delay US approvals and warrants monitoring.
filings.impactWhy: US FDA classified subsidiary's facility as Official Action Indicated (OAI).

filings.headline: Object clause altered, CIN changed after shareholder nod at Sept 2026 AGM
filings.summary: JNK India changed its CIN from L29268MH2010PLC204223 to L28150MH2010PLC204223 following alteration of the Object Clause of its Memorandum of Association, approved by shareholders at the AGM on September 25, 2026 and recorded by the RoC on November 16, 2026. A change in business objects signals a potential expansion or shift in the company's permitted activities. The filing gives no financial details of any new business line.
filings.impactWhy: Routine object clause alteration and CIN change.

filings.headline: Aether to build India's first dedicated DRA plant for Baker Hughes unit
filings.summary: Aether signed a long-term Facility Development and Supply Agreement with Baker Petrolite LLC (a Baker Hughes company) to build and operate a dedicated plant at Site Magnum (Site 5), Panoli, as its exclusive manufacturing supplier for Drag Reducing Agents. No deal size is disclosed, but the agreement opens a new end-market in energy infrastructure and is India's first dedicated DRA facility, giving long-term revenue visibility. Baker Petrolite is an existing customer; the deal is at arm's length and not a related-party transaction.
filings.impactWhy: Supply and facility agreement without disclosed contract value.

filings.headline: Subsidiary signs binding EOI to buy up to 26% of A-Thon, enters Land Systems
filings.summary: Apollo Defence Industries (ADIPL), a subsidiary, signed a binding Expression of Interest to acquire up to 26% of A-Thon Allterrain Private Limited, with intent to raise the stake in further tranches at the same valuation. A-Thon makes all-terrain and side-by-side utility vehicles under an Industrial Licence, marking the Apollo Group's entry into a new Land Systems vertical. Consideration and structure are to be set after due diligence; it opens a new business line though it remains subject to definitive agreements and approvals.
filings.impactWhy: Non-final binding EOI for minority 26% stake without disclosed valuation.

filings.headline: TCPL forms JV with Italy's Brandart for Asia-Pacific packaging, via Singapore entity
filings.summary: TCPL signed a Joint Venture Agreement with Brandart S.p.A., Italy, to explore premium packaging opportunities across the Asia-Pacific region, via a private company to be incorporated in Singapore. The investment amount will be determined later per the JV terms and opportunity identified, so no financial figures are disclosed. It opens a new strategic international partnership combining TCPL's manufacturing with Brandart's global premium-brand relationships.
filings.impactWhy: Joint venture agreement without disclosed financials or investment size.

filings.headline: Group CFO & Executive Director Anand Sharma resigns, effective Nov 16, 2026
filings.summary: Mr. Anand H. Sharma has ceased to be Executive Director and Group CFO (KMP) with effect from close of business on November 16, 2026, citing inability to relocate to the Bhavnagar headquarters under the 'Carysil 2.0' plan. filings.impactWhy: Resignation of Group CFO and Executive Director.

filings.headline: Sigma forms India JV with Spain's EM&E Group for defence manufacturing
filings.summary: Sigma Advanced Systems announced a strategic joint venture, headquartered in India and already operational, with Spain's Escribano Mechanical & Engineering (EM&E Group) to localise, manufacture and co-develop advanced defence systems including remote-controlled weapon systems, ammunition guidance and electro-optics. The deal marks Sigma's shift from components/subsystems maker to a broader aerospace and defence systems platform, a new business line. The filing also notes a reconstituted Board, with Lt Gen B.S. Raju (Retd.) as Chairman and new independent directors.
filings.impactWhy: Joint venture announcement without disclosed financial investment size.

filings.headline: Won 2nd Nawada quartzite block; combined 17.48 lakh MTPA capacity, ₹274.5cr over 5yrs
filings.summary: Monolithisch India was allotted a 2nd quartzite stone block adjacent to its existing Nawada block via Bihar e-auction, with combined approved capacity of 17.48 lakh MTPA (new block 10.38 lakh MTPA). Total royalty-inclusive consideration is ₹274.50cr over 5 years, with mining targeted to start April 2027. The expanded raw-material base supports planned diversification into foundry-grade, glass-grade and speciality silica and tile adhesives, a strategic expansion against ₹179cr yearly sales.
filings.impactWhy: Quartzite stone block auction win spread over 5 years.

filings.headline: Postal ballot to migrate shares from NSE Emerge to Main Board of NSE/BSE
filings.summary: Alpex Solar has issued a postal ballot notice (special resolution) seeking member approval to migrate its equity listing from the NSE Emerge SME platform to the Main Board of NSE and/or BSE when eligible. E-voting runs Nov 18 to Dec 17, 2026, with results by Dec 19, 2026. A main-board migration typically improves liquidity, index eligibility and institutional visibility for the ₹1,652cr company.
filings.impactWhy: Postal ballot to approve future migration from SME to Main Board.

filings.headline: QIP completed: ₹3,500cr raised via 2.89cr shares at ₹1,210
filings.summary: Aegis Logistics allotted 2,89,25,619 equity shares at ₹1,210 each (face value ₹1) to 33 QIBs, raising ₹3,500 crore. The issue expands share capital from 35.10cr to 37.99cr shares — about 8.2% more shares and roughly 7.6% dilution to existing holders; issue price of ₹1,210 is just below the current ₹1,228.1. Largest allottees were Smallcap World Fund (33.2%), Quant Mutual Fund (31.4% PAN-clubbed) and New World Fund (14.2%).
filings.impactWhy: QIP dilution of ~7.6% exceeds the 5% threshold.

filings.headline: Sai Parenterals to buy majority stake in Bion Therapeutics via subsidiary
filings.summary: Board approved acquiring a majority/controlling stake in Hyderabad-based branded formulations firm Bion Therapeutics (India) Pvt Ltd through wholly owned subsidiary SP Analytics, making Bion a step-down subsidiary. Bion had FY25-26 total income of ₹47.29cr and ₹28.75cr in H1 FY27 (~7% of the company's ₹668cr yearly sales). It is an all-cash deal funded via IPO GCP proceeds and debt, expected to close by 30 November 2026; consideration will be set by an independent valuer and is not disclosed.
filings.impactWhy: Acquisition target accounts for only ~7% of annual sales.

filings.headline: Khalapur helium plant live; Q2 revenue up 31.8% to ₹139.4cr
filings.summary: Stallion commissioned its Khalapur High-Purity Helium Facility, entering high-value specialty gases (semiconductors, MRI, aerospace, defence) with a SOC Dubai/Qatar sourcing alliance. Q2 FY27 revenue rose 31.8% YoY to ₹139.37cr and H1 revenue 22.1% to ₹264.05cr, with H1 operating PAT (pre-ESOP) up 40.2% to ₹30.53cr. The new business line plus double-digit growth is positive; this is a revised release superseding the Nov 15 version with no change to the financials.
filings.impactWhy: Revised release with no change to previously reported financials.

filings.headline: Pace Digitek wins ₹2,691cr BESS order from NTPC Green, largest-ever
filings.summary: Pace Digitek received a Letter of Award worth Rs. 26,913 million (Rs. 2,691 crore incl. GST) from NTPC Green Energy for a 600 MW/1800 MWh BESS EPC and 15-year O&M project at Khavda, Gujarat. The order equals roughly 87% of last 12 months' sales (~₹3104cr) and is the company's largest-ever BESS win. It lifts FY2027 order inflows to Rs. 5,129 crore and total executable order book to Rs. 13,427 crore.
filings.impactWhy: Order win equals ~87% of yearly sales.

filings.headline: Q2 consol revenue ₹399cr, EBITDA up 35% to ₹58cr; Egypt plant started
filings.summary: Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose to ₹399cr (vs ₹360cr), EBITDA up 35% YoY to ₹58cr (margin 15%) and PAT ₹20cr (vs ₹14cr). India revenue grew 10% YoY to ₹255cr and USA revenue rose 29% to ₹112cr. New Egypt facility commenced commercial production of CNG cylinders in Sept 2026 with dispatches in October, and the Egyptian subsidiary signed an MoU with CARGAS to explore CNG transport unit manufacturing.
filings.impactWhy: Routine quarterly results and past commercial production commencement.

filings.headline: Q2FY27 PAT ₹133cr (down 10% YoY); H1 revenue up 19% to ₹2,497cr; FY27 guidance kept
filings.summary: Standalone Q2FY27 revenue was ₹1,132.6cr (flat vs ₹1,149cr YoY, down 17% QoQ) with PAT of ₹133.3cr vs ₹148.2cr, while H1FY27 revenue rose 19.4% to ₹2,497.4cr and PAT 7% to ₹296.1cr. Operating cash flow turned positive at ₹127cr (vs ₹158cr outflow), order book stands at ₹22,634cr, and the company reaffirmed FY27 guidance of ₹6,000-6,500cr revenue and 18% EBITDA margin. Guidance maintained with strong revenue visibility, though Q2 profit declined YoY on margin moderation and higher depreciation/finance costs.
filings.impactWhy: Guidance was merely reaffirmed, not changed.

filings.headline: Postal ballot to revise IPO-fund use: all 19 IVF centres pushed to FY29
filings.summary: Gaudium IVF seeks shareholder approval via postal ballot (voting Nov 17–Dec 16, 2026) to vary the objects of its IPO offer, changing locations and revising the schedule for the 19 planned new IVF centres, now targeted for completion by Fiscal 2029 (10 in FY27, 8 in FY28, 1 in FY29). The ₹50cr allocation under Object No. 1 is unchanged, with ₹36.52cr of net proceeds still unutilised as on Sep 30, 2026. The revised timeline and location substitutions signal a slower rollout of the IPO-funded expansion.
filings.impactWhy: Revision to IPO proceeds deployment timeline.

filings.headline: Promoters to sell up to 3.44% (~₹616cr) to meet minimum public shareholding
filings.summary: Four promoters (Paritosh Kumar, Ashish Garg and two HUFs) intend to sell up to 32,47,750 shares (3.44% of equity) in the open market between Nov 17-24, 2026 to comply with minimum public shareholding norms. At ~₹1,895 the stake is worth about ₹616cr. Promoter and promoter-group holding stands at 78.44% as on Nov 16, 2026, well above the 75% cap, so this sale reduces it toward ~75%.
filings.impactWhy: Promoters selling up to 3.44% stake.

filings.headline: All Time Plastics' arm starts engineered bamboo board plant in Assam
filings.summary: Wholly owned subsidiary All Time Bamboo Pvt Ltd commenced operations of an Engineered Bamboo Board Manufacturing Facility at Madanpur, North Guwahati, Assam, on a 75,700 sq ft leased shed with installed capacity of 3,000 cubic metres per annum. This marks entry into a new product line beyond the company's existing plastics business. Capacity commencement and a new business segment are positive for growth, though revenue contribution is not quantified.
filings.impactWhy: Plant commencement with unquantified revenue impact.

filings.headline: Capacite wins ₹670cr CIDCO housing order, ~24% of yearly sales
filings.summary: Capacite received a Letter of Acceptance from CIDCO for ₹670.43cr (excl GST) to construct the MAHA Awas DRS Housing Scheme at CBD-Belapur, Navi Mumbai, over 42 months. The order equals about 24% of last 12 months' sales of ₹2787cr, a sizeable addition to the order book. Management calls it a repeat mandate from CIDCO, strengthening its public-sector presence and future revenue visibility.
filings.impactWhy: Order win equals ~24% of annual sales.

filings.headline: Bags ₹325cr LOA from Chittaranjan Loco Works for 156 IGBT propulsion sets
filings.summary: MV Electrosystems received a letter of acceptance worth ₹325.26cr (incl GST) from Chittaranjan Locomotive Works for 156 sets of IGBT-based 3-phase drive propulsion equipment for WAG9/WAG9H/WAP7/WAP5 locomotives, with deliveries from April 2027 to January 2028 plus a 3-year comprehensive maintenance provision. The order is very large relative to the company's reported trailing sales and is a significant domestic railway win.
filings.impactWhy: Order win is very large relative to company's annual sales.

filings.headline: Hirect wins ₹133.38cr CLW order for IGBT propulsion systems (~12% of sales)
filings.summary: Hirect received a Letter of Acceptance from Chittaranjan Locomotive Works for 78 sets of IGBT-based 3-phase propulsion equipment valued at ₹133.38 crore, with deliveries from April 2027 to February 2028 plus three years of annual maintenance. The order is about 11.8% of the ₹1131cr annual sales, strengthening its position as an RDSO UVAM-approved development source for railway propulsion.
filings.impactWhy: Order win equals ~12% of annual sales.

filings.headline: Q2 FY27 consol revenue ₹198cr, up 143% YoY; EBITDA ₹17.4cr, up 433%
filings.summary: TIL reported Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue of ₹197.79cr (up 143% YoY, 68% QoQ) with EBITDA of ₹17.37cr at an 8.8% margin, aided by the first full quarter of TCPL; net loss narrowed to ₹1.31cr from ₹7.73cr. Standalone revenue rose ~29% YoY to ₹101cr with ₹12.64cr EBITDA and a return to cash profit after five quarters. Combined order book of ₹534cr (plus ₹276cr pipeline, ₹217cr enquiries) against ~₹377cr yearly sales gives strong H2 execution visibility.
filings.impactWhy: Quarterly earnings release without guidance revision.

filings.headline: Received provisional completion certificate for ₹1,589cr HAM highway project
filings.summary: Dilip Buildcon received the Provisional Completion Certificate for its ₹1,589 crore Maradgi S Andola-Baswantpur 6-lane greenfield HAM highway (NH-150C, Bharatmala). Completion came on the 912th day from the appointed date of 24-04-2023, against a scheduled date of 24-08-2026. The project cost is about 17.5% of ₹9,066cr yearly sales, and early/on-time completion supports annuity collection and bonus eligibility.
filings.impactWhy: Routine provisional completion certificate for HAM project.

filings.headline: TACC signs non-binding MoU with global OEM for fast-charging anode supply
filings.summary: HEG's wholly owned subsidiary TACC Limited signed a non-binding MoU with a global automotive OEM to explore supply of fast-charging anode materials for EVs, potentially covering up to 30% of Phase 1 capacity (20,000 MT/year) at its Dewas plant. The MoU only sets a framework for further commercial negotiations and carries no firm order value. It matters as an early validation of HEG's new battery-materials business line, though it is exploratory and non-binding.
filings.impactWhy: Non-binding MoU with no committed order value.

filings.headline: KPIL bags ₹2,610cr power T&D order in South America
filings.summary: KPIL secured a notification of award for an EPC order worth ~₹2,610 crore for power transmission lines and substations in the international (South America) market. The order is about 9.4% of FY26 revenue (₹27,143cr) and ~9% of LTM sales of ₹27,855cr. YTD FY27 order inflows now exceed ₹26,000cr, up over 50% year-on-year.
filings.impactWhy: Order win is ~9% of annual sales, below 10% threshold.

filings.headline: H1 FY27 PAT -53% to ₹852mn despite 18% revenue growth; order book ₹10,625cr
filings.summary: Kaynes' H1 FY27 revenue rose 18% YoY to ₹18,987mn, but PAT fell 53% to ₹852mn and Q2 PAT dropped 66% to ₹398mn as EBITDA margin slipped to 14.1% (from 16.1%). Working capital days jumped to 169 from 123 and debt/equity rose to 0.4x from 0.2x, signalling a sharp profitability and cash-cycle deterioration. Offsetting this, the order book grew 31% YoY to ₹106,252mn (about 2.7x yearly sales), supporting medium-term visibility.
filings.impactWhy: Quarterly financial results without management exit or guidance change.

filings.headline: Q2 PAT ₹23.5cr up 32%; order book up 94% to ₹2,531cr; CARE upgrade to A
filings.summary: DEE reported Q2 FY27 PAT of ₹23.5cr (up 31.8% YoY) and revenue of ₹293cr (up 8.5%), with EBITDA margin at 20.1%; closing order book rose 93.5% YoY to ₹2,531cr (vs ₹1,308cr), led by Power and Oil & Gas. CareEdge upgraded the long-term rating to CARE A (from A-) and short-term to A1 (from A2+) on ₹1,474cr of facilities, and the company reaffirmed FY27 revenue guidance of ₹1,500cr versus LTM sales of ₹1,213cr. ₹225cr of debt was repaid from the ₹300cr July preferential issue, aiding deleveraging and a nuclear-piping push.
filings.impactWhy: Credit rating upgraded to CARE A from CARE A-.

filings.headline: Q2FY27 turnaround: PAT +₹32cr, revenue ₹4,320cr (+23% QoQ), EBITDA +270%
filings.summary: Allcargo Global reported Q2FY27 consolidated revenue of ₹4,320cr, up 23% QoQ from ₹3,522cr, with EBITDA rising to ₹122cr from ₹33cr (+270% QoQ) and PBT of ₹62cr. Profit After Tax turned positive at ₹32cr versus a ₹28cr loss in Q1FY27, driven by yield improvement, cost control and higher LCL, FCL and Air volumes. The return to profitability after prior-quarter losses is a meaningful positive signal for the investment case.
filings.impactWhy: Routine quarterly earnings turnaround.

filings.headline: Launches 'The Bungalows' Gurugram luxury project, ~₹4,000cr GDV
filings.summary: Max Estates launched the first phase of 'The Bungalows' on ~7.25 acres in Gurugram Sector 59, with 243 luxury residences across two towers. The project has an estimated overall Gross Development Value of ~₹4,000 crore, roughly 20x the company's ₹204cr annual sales, adding significant future revenue potential to its LiveWell residential portfolio.
filings.impactWhy: Routine real estate project launch.

filings.headline: H1 FY27 revenue ₹242.96cr (up 86.8%), PAT ₹20.08cr; FY27 guided ~2x H1
filings.summary: MaxVolt reported H1 FY27 revenue of ₹242.96cr (up 86.8% YoY) and PAT of ₹20.08cr (8.26% margin), with EBITDA of ₹28.98cr; H1 revenue alone is 81.9% of full-year FY26's ₹296.76cr. Management guided FY27 to close at nearly 2x H1 revenue (~₹485cr), implying continued strong growth versus ₹404cr trailing sales. Duhai's 2.3GWh plant is operational and a 10GWh Aligarh plant is under construction.
filings.impactWhy: Routine earnings update and operational growth targets.

filings.headline: Promoter bought 0.04% (₹5.9cr) at about ₹784
filings.summary: Promoter entity Riddhi Portfolio Private Limited bought 75,000 shares (0.04% of the company) through market purchases for ₹5.9 crore at an average price of ₹784, close to the current price of ₹785. Their holding remains at 34.2% (34.2% before to 34.2% after).
filings.impactWhy: Promoter entity purchased shares in the company.

filings.headline: Alembic gets USFDA final nod for Binimetinib Tablets with 180-day exclusivity
filings.summary: Alembic received USFDA final approval for its ANDA for Binimetinib Tablets 15 mg and 45 mg, generic to Mektovi. As one of the first/sole first applicants with paragraph IV certification, it is eligible for 180 days of generic exclusivity. The drug has an estimated US market size of US$282 million for the twelve months ending September 2026 (IQVIA), meaningful against ₹8477cr yearly sales, making this a valuable launch opportunity.
filings.impactWhy: US FDA final approval with 180-day exclusivity on $282M market drug.

filings.headline: 9 GW TOPCon cell facility to produce first cell Dec 2026; EBITDA/watt +37% QoQ
filings.summary: Q2/H1 FY27 results: H1 revenue up 17.7% YoY, absolute EBITDA per watt up 37% QoQ despite lower volumes, and 1.7 GW of new orders added (vs 0.8 GW in Q1). The 9 GW N-type TOPCon cell facility at Gangaikondan is on track to produce its first cell in December 2026, with ingot/wafer capacity by FY29 and a 7.5 GWh BESS plant due January 2027. Business mix improved (DCR 7.5%→22%, distribution/retail 14%→44%); net debt/equity at 0.17x.
filings.impactWhy: Routine quarterly performance and ongoing facility construction update.

filings.headline: Q2 FY27 revenue up 90.3% to ₹1,311cr, PAT up 129.6% to ₹33.2cr; ₹0.40 dividend
filings.summary: Skyways reported consolidated Q2 FY27 revenue from operations of ₹1,311.45cr (up 90.3% YoY) and PAT of ₹33.18cr (up 129.6%), with H1 PAT of ₹59.97cr and basic EPS of ₹1.91 for the quarter. The Board declared a second interim dividend of ₹0.40 per share (record date 20 Nov 2026), and the company retained its No.1 rank in Indian air exports with market share rising to 6.3%. Strong growth and improving margins (PAT margin 2.53%) support the investment case.
filings.impactWhy: Quarterly financial results without qualifying extraordinary events.

filings.headline: Q2FY27 net profit crashes ~97% YoY to ₹3.7cr on flat sales
filings.summary: Standalone Q2FY27 revenue was ₹1,073.3cr (vs ₹1,109.9cr YoY) but net profit collapsed to ₹3.7cr from ₹128.2cr a year earlier, with H1 profit down to ₹22.5cr from ₹262.7cr. Margins were squeezed as depreciation jumped to ₹65.5cr (from ₹34.9cr) and finance costs rose to ₹42.3cr. Auditors also flag ₹148.5cr safeguard duty treated as receivable and ₹52.8cr of disputed EPC receivables under arbitration.
filings.impactWhy: Quarterly results with flat sales; profit drop alone does not qualify.

filings.headline: Q2 FY27 revenue ₹100.7cr (+29% YoY); net loss narrows to ₹1.7cr
filings.summary: TIL reported standalone Q2 (Sep 2026) revenue of ₹100.66cr, up from ₹78.27cr a year earlier, with a net loss of ₹1.71cr versus a ₹7.72cr loss in Q2 FY26. H1 revenue was ₹179.3cr (vs ₹141.2cr) with a loss of ₹8.87cr, narrowing from ₹13.94cr. Auditors flagged an emphasis of matter on deferred tax asset recognition; the company remains loss-making despite improving sales against its ₹377cr annual revenue.
filings.impactWhy: Routine quarterly financial results.

filings.headline: Q2 FY27 income ₹391cr up 169% YoY; PAT ₹44.55cr up 70.8%
filings.summary: Fineotex reported Q2 FY27 total income of ₹391.41cr (up 169.1% YoY) and H1 income of ₹778.13cr (up 166.8% YoY), with Q2 PAT of ₹44.55cr and H1 PAT of ₹92.75cr. Operating EBITDA was ₹59.59cr in Q2 and ₹118.74cr in H1, with H1 volumes up ~132.3%, driven largely by the US oil & gas acquisition (53.33% stake in CrudeChem) and new US water-treatment platform. The scale jump materially reshapes the business versus ₹1013cr trailing sales.
filings.impactWhy: Sharply higher quarterly revenue (+169%) and volumes (+132%).

filings.headline: Q2FY27 standalone revenue ₹759cr, net profit ₹39.2cr (up 40% YoY)
filings.summary: Board approved unaudited Q2/H1 FY27 results; standalone revenue from operations was ₹758.75cr (Q2FY26: ₹710.86cr) and net profit ₹39.2cr (Q2FY26: ₹28.0cr), with EPS of ₹0.75. H1 revenue stood at ₹1,437.18cr and profit ₹60.78cr versus ₹31.08cr a year ago. Results carry a clean limited review from Walker Chandiok & Co LLP.
filings.impactWhy: Routine quarterly financial results.

filings.headline: Vikram Kumar Khaitan appointed CFO
filings.summary: EPACK Prefab's board approved the appointment of Mr. Vikram Kumar Khaitan as Chief Financial Officer (KMP) effective November 14, 2026. A Chartered Accountant and Company Secretary with over two decades of experience, he was most recently CFO of Kuantum Papers Limited. CFO appointments are material as a key managerial change.
filings.impactWhy: Appointment of Chief Financial Officer.

filings.headline: KIMS arm to manage 250-bed Westfort Hospital, Kerala; ₹50L/month or 9% of revenue
filings.summary: KSPL, a wholly-owned subsidiary, signed a 10-year O&M agreement (extendable 5 years) for exclusive rights to run the 250-bed Westfort Hi-Tech Hospital in Thrissur, Kerala, earning ₹50 lakh/month or 9% of net revenue. The fee (~₹6cr/year) is small versus ₹4597cr yearly sales, but it marks KIMS's entry/expansion into the Kerala market and extends its brand footprint. Not a related-party transaction.
filings.impactWhy: Hospital O&M agreement value is minor relative to yearly sales.

filings.headline: Galaxy signs MoU with LG Electronics to co-develop sustainable cleaning solutions
filings.summary: Galaxy Surfactants signed a Memorandum of Understanding with LG Electronics to co-develop and commercialize next-generation sustainable cleaning solutions. The filing gives no financial figures, volumes or timelines, and an MoU is non-binding. Still, a long-term partnership with a global technology leader could open a new product avenue over time.
filings.impactWhy: Non-binding MoU with no financial commitments specified.

filings.headline: Solex bags ₹628cr module order (~39% of yearly sales); order book over ₹4,000cr
filings.summary: Solex secured a ₹628.37cr order from a global renewable group for N-Type TOPCon G12R modules, its largest of FY27, plus smaller orders of ₹42.47cr, ₹74.77cr, ₹75.96cr and ₹194.14cr; total order book visibility exceeds ₹4,000cr (₹1,050cr confirmed with advances). The flagship order alone is about 39% of ₹1,619cr yearly sales. Q2 FY27 revenue rose 75.8% YoY to ₹2,743mn but PAT fell 32.7% YoY to ₹39mn on a regulatory procurement pause; a subsidiary also approved a ₹150cr CCD issuance.
filings.impactWhy: Order win of ₹628cr represents ~39% of yearly sales.

filings.headline: Saudi cancels WABAG's ₹2,332cr desalination order (55% of yearly sales)
filings.summary: Saudi Water Authority cancelled the 300 MLD Yanbu sea-water desalination tender worth USD 272 Million (SAR 1,019 Million / INR 2,332 Crores), citing internal reasons on its side, after WABAG had executed the contract. The order was about 55% of last 12 months' sales of ₹4,262cr, so its loss is a major setback to the order book. WABAG says it is approaching the customer to understand the reasons and next steps.
filings.impactWhy: Cancellation of ₹2,332cr contract representing 55% of yearly sales.

filings.headline: H1 FY27 revenue up 28% to ₹1,000cr, PAT ₹135cr; wins ₹3,870cr BESS order
filings.summary: H1 FY27 consolidated revenue from operations rose 28% YoY to ₹999.9cr (₹781.2cr prior) with PAT of ₹134.6cr (up 11%) and EBITDA ₹249.4cr (up 33%); EPS ₹13.35. Notable wins include two MSEDCL awards for 900MW/1,800MWh battery storage worth ₹3,870cr over 15 years (more than yearly sales), a 50MW Rajasthan solar EPC, and a ₹501cr sale of a 110MWp C&I portfolio to Actis. Also signed a ₹4,500cr green hydrogen/ammonia/methanol MoU with Maharashtra; CRISIL A-/Stable reaffirmed.
filings.impactWhy: Secured ₹3,870cr battery storage order exceeding annual sales.

filings.headline: CFO Malkit Singh Bharaj resigns; Rajinder Singh named new CFO from Nov 15
filings.summary: CFO Malkit Singh Bharaj resigned effective close of business Nov 14, 2026 (moving to Group Finance Director role), with Rajinder Singh appointed CFO from Nov 15, 2026. Whole Time Director Charanjit Singh resigned from that post and was re-designated as a Non-Executive Director. The board also re-appointed two independent directors and cleared a wholly owned subsidiary, but the CFO change is the key senior-management move.
filings.impactWhy: Resignation and appointment of Chief Financial Officer.

filings.headline: H1 FY27 revenue +50%, net profit +76%; guides 30-35% FY27 growth
filings.summary: United Heat Transfer reported H1 FY27 revenue of ₹321.9 Mn (+50.1% YoY), EBITDA ₹38.1 Mn (+49.1%, margin steady at 11.9%) and net profit ₹14.7 Mn (+75.5%). It guides to 30-35% revenue growth for FY27 and holds orders worth ₹499.7 Mn (~₹50cr, ~36% of ₹140cr yearly sales) under execution for the rest of FY27. Working capital days improved sharply to ~264 from ~442, supporting the positive outlook.
filings.impactWhy: Mid-year results and regular execution updates.

filings.headline: Corrects error: consolidated H1 basic EPS cut from ₹12.82 to ₹9.59
filings.summary: Rishabh flagged inadvertent errors in EPS reported in its Q2/H1 FY27 consolidated results and revised them down: Q2 basic EPS ₹4.69→₹4.66, H1 basic EPS ₹12.82→₹9.59 and H1 diluted ₹12.70→₹9.50. It says no other financial figures change, so underlying profit (standalone H1 profit ₹254.01mn) is unaffected, but a ~25% overstatement of headline consolidated H1 EPS points to a reporting-control lapse worth watching.
filings.impactWhy: Correction of reporting error; underlying profit unaffected.

filings.headline: Warburg Pincus to buy 38.51% of demerged Pricol Autotech from promoters
filings.summary: Pricol's board approved a share purchase agreement under which Warburg Pincus affiliate Topaz Terrace Investments will acquire 4,69,34,833 shares (38.51% on fully diluted basis) of Pricol Autotech from promoters/sellers. Pricol Autotech holds the demerged Driver Information & Connected Vehicle Solutions business; completion follows the demerger becoming effective, listing, an open offer under SAST and CCI approval. Post-deal Warburg gains control of Pricol Autotech and the sellers exit its promoter group, though there is no change in control of Pricol Limited itself.
filings.impactWhy: Promoters selling 38.51% stake to Warburg Pincus in demerged entity.

filings.headline: Warburg Pincus to buy 38.51% of demerged Pricol Autotech from promoters
filings.summary: Pricol's board approved a Share Purchase Agreement under which Topaz Terrace Investments (a Warburg Pincus affiliate) will acquire 4,69,34,833 shares (38.51% on a fully diluted basis) of Pricol Autotech from the Mohan promoter group and group entities. The stake relates to shares to be allotted under the earlier-approved demerger of the Driver Information & Connected Vehicle Solutions business into Pricol Autotech. Completion is subject to the demerger becoming effective, listing of Pricol Autotech, a mandatory open offer, and CCI approval; it brings in a new institutional controlling shareholder for the demerged entity, with no change to control of Pricol Limited.
filings.impactWhy: Promoters selling 38.51% stake to Warburg Pincus in demerged entity.

filings.headline: Q2FY27 revenue +19.5% to ₹558.4cr but PAT -23.7% to ₹44.6cr on margin squeeze
filings.summary: Q2FY27 revenue from operations rose 19.5% YoY to ₹5,584mn (₹558cr) on improved realizations, but EBITDA fell 21.0% to ₹736mn and PAT dropped 23.7% to ₹446mn as EBITDA margin compressed to 13.2% from 19.9%. H1FY27 PAT was down 12.4% to ₹710mn, with management citing raw material cost pressures, supply challenges and weaker high-margin product sales. Below-normal monsoon and El Niño risk to rabi sowing could further weigh on crop-protection demand.
filings.impactWhy: Quarterly results with margin compression; no record performance.

filings.headline: India Ratings upgrades long-term rating to IND AA from IND AA-; A1+ affirmed
filings.summary: India Ratings upgraded Sai Life Sciences' bank loan facilities (₹7,690mn limits) long-term rating to IND AA/Stable from IND AA-/Positive, while affirming the short-term rating at IND A1+. The upgrade reflects sustained business/financial profile improvement, with FY26 revenue of ₹21,925mn, EBITDA margin of 29% and net leverage at 0.2x. A rating upgrade lowers funding costs and supports the planned ₹11-13bn FY27 capex.
filings.impactWhy: Credit rating upgraded to IND AA from IND AA-.

filings.headline: Q2 swings to ₹66.7cr net loss vs ₹65.3cr profit; revenue down 22% YoY
filings.summary: Consolidated Q2FY27 revenue from operations fell to ₹507.37cr from ₹652.65cr a year earlier, and the company posted a net loss of ₹66.73cr versus a profit of ₹65.27cr. H1 net loss was ₹124.61cr against a ₹88.68cr profit last year, with EBIT turning negative (pre-tax loss ₹132.22cr). The sharp swing to losses on falling sales is a clear red flag for the investment case.
filings.impactWhy: Quarterly loss and revenue decline without record metric.

filings.headline: Shail Jayesh Shah appointed CFO (KMP) effective Nov 13, 2026
filings.summary: At its Nov 13, 2026 board meeting, GSP Crop Science appointed Mr. Shail Jayesh Shah, a Whole-Time Director, as Chief Financial Officer (KMP) effective immediately. The board also approved Q2/H1 FY27 results (Q2 revenue ₹5,992.49mn), and separately noted a corporate office shift within Ahmedabad and the retirement of the Head of International Business. The CFO appointment is the key material event; the office relocation is routine.
filings.impactWhy: Appointment of new Chief Financial Officer.

filings.headline: Q2FY27 revenue +96% to ₹837cr but PAT falls 32% to ₹25cr on margin squeeze
filings.summary: H1FY27 revenue doubled YoY to ₹1,582.09cr and EBITDA rose 23.3% to ₹140.31cr, but Q2FY27 net profit fell 32.18% YoY to ₹25.06cr (PAT margin 3.00% vs 8.68%) as EBITDA margin dropped to 7.58% from 13.15% on industry pricing and input costs plus higher depreciation and finance costs from INA3 commissioning. Management guides to full-year FY27 EBITDA and margins recovering to FY26 levels, with a ~2.2 GW order book (1.3 GW for delivery by March 2027) and the 4.5 GW TOPCon cell line targeting first operations in Q4FY27. Strong top-line visibility is offset by near-term profitability pressure.
filings.impactWhy: Quarterly results with lower margins; typical earnings filing.

filings.headline: Pennar bags ₹1,430cr orders (~39% of sales); Q2 PBT up 24% to ₹50.9cr
filings.summary: Pennar Industries received orders worth INR 1,430 Crore across PEB, Boilers, ICD, Steel, Tubes and Railway verticals over the last three months, to be executed in coming quarters. This is about 39% of the ₹3,645cr yearly sales, a sizeable order inflow. The filing also reported Q2FY27 consolidated total income of INR 1,029.25 Crore (up 11.92%) and PBT of INR 50.89 Crore (up 24.30%).
filings.impactWhy: Order win of ₹1,430cr represents ~39% of yearly sales.

filings.headline: Q2 FY27 revenue up 38% to ₹3,687cr, PAT doubles to ₹36.5cr; targets double profits
filings.summary: TVS SCS reported Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue of ₹3,687.2cr (up 38.5% YoY), EBITDA of ₹268.1cr (up 50.2%, margin 7.3% vs 6.7%), and PAT of ₹36.5cr (up 123.9%). Management guided to over 20% revenue growth across both segments and aims to double profits in FY27, backed by an ₹8,200cr order pipeline. Strong broad-based growth with GFS EBITDA margin up 170bps supports the earnings-quality story.
filings.impactWhy: Quarterly financial results and broad aspirational profit target.

filings.headline: Q2FY27 revenue +21% to ₹2,370cr but PAT -74% to ₹31cr on margin squeeze
filings.summary: Jubilant Pharmova reported Q2'FY27 revenue of ₹2,370 Cr (up 21% YoY) but EBITDA fell 27% to ₹255 Cr (margin 10.7% vs 17.8%) and reported PAT dropped 74% to ₹31 Cr. H1'FY27 PAT was ₹87 Cr vs ₹222 Cr. Profitability was hit by loss of high-margin SPECT radiopharma products and remediation costs at CMO Montreal; it also raised ₹800 Cr via NCDs for refinancing and capex.
filings.impactWhy: Quarterly financial results showing margin squeeze.

filings.headline: Auditors of two material subsidiaries resign to align with parent rotation
filings.summary: Walker Chandiok & Co LLP and V G G C & Associates resigned as statutory auditors of material subsidiaries Shriprop Properties and Global Entropolis (Vizag) effective November 13, 2026. The resignations are to align with the parent's statutory auditor following mandatory auditor rotation at Shriram Properties, with no disputes or audit concerns cited. Auditor resignations warrant attention, though reasons are procedural.
filings.impactWhy: Routine resignation of subsidiary auditors due to mandatory rotation.

filings.headline: Court passes ex-parte order; property attachment, ₹8.27cr security demand
filings.summary: UC Inclusive Credit obtained an ex-parte ad-interim order (Bengaluru Civil Court) requiring GBL and ABPL to show cause by Dec 4, 2026 why they shouldn't furnish security of ₹8.27cr, with a conditional attachment on certain company properties. The claim stems from an alleged ₹5cr corporate guarantee the company says is forged (part of unauthorised transactions by its former CEO); NCLT already dismissed related insolvency proceedings in July 2026. The company states no expected financial implications and plans to appeal, but the attachment of properties and ongoing fraud litigation (~1.9% of ₹433cr sales) is a live risk.
filings.impactWhy: Ad-interim court security demand of ₹8.27cr is relatively small.

filings.headline: Q2 FY27 Adj PAT up 25% to ₹166cr; enters electronics, aerospace via new orders
filings.summary: Belrise reported Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue of ₹2,746cr (+16.7% YoY) and adjusted PAT of ₹166cr (+25% YoY), with manufacturing revenue up 26%. It opened new business lines: a maiden LoI for CNC fixtures from an ecosystem partner of a large American smartphone company, a first incremental aerospace track-beam order via UK subsidiary Chester Hall, and a Yamato (Japan) filtration tech licence. New auto orders (CV chassis, 3W body) carry peak annual revenue potential of ₹150-200cr and ₹100-120cr, small versus ~₹9,794cr yearly sales, but the diversification beyond automotive is strategically significant.
filings.impactWhy: Quarterly results; new orders are small relative to total revenue.

filings.headline: CFO Azim Syed to exit; Abhishek Bajaj named CFO & CIRO from 1 Jan 2027
filings.summary: Azim Syed, current CFO and CIRO, moves to a global role at RHI Magnesita Vienna effective 1 January 2027, and Abhishek Bajaj (currently CFO of RHI Magnesita India Refractories Ltd) is appointed CFO & CIRO from the same date. A CFO-level change is material. The release also reports Q2 FY27 revenue of ₹1,030cr (-0.5% YoY), EBITDA ₹144cr (+30%) and PAT ₹62cr (+62% YoY).
filings.impactWhy: Exit of current CFO and appointment of new CFO.

filings.headline: Monitoring agency flags fund comingling in ₹594.84cr QIP use
filings.summary: CARE Ratings' Q2FY27 monitoring report on Zaggle's ₹594.84cr QIP found delays in deploying funds for strategic investments/acquisitions and general corporate purposes without board approval. Funds for the acquisitions object were moved to a current account with other business transactions, causing comingling; of ₹75cr GCP reimbursement, ₹40.82cr pertains to Q1FY27 and was routed through the cash credit account. No material deviation from objects was declared, but the governance lapses around fund handling are a red flag.
filings.impactWhy: Monitoring agency report flagging procedural QIP fund routing issues.

filings.headline: Board approves merger of H One India into Belrise; Q2 net profit ₹166cr
filings.summary: Board approved a Scheme of Amalgamation of H One India Private Limited into Belrise Industries, plus an SPV under the PM SETU project and an amendment to the related-party transactions policy. Q2 consolidated revenue was ₹2,746cr (up from ₹2,354cr a year ago) with net profit of ₹166cr versus ₹133cr; detailed terms of the merger will be disclosed in due course. The merger could reshape the standalone entity, though the swap ratio and size are not yet given.
filings.impactWhy: Merger announced without key swap terms or financial details.

filings.headline: Q2 FY27 segment guidance: bathware mid-teen growth, appliances ₹500cr+ in 2 yrs
filings.summary: Hindware's business-wise update sets FY27 targets: mid-teen bathware revenue growth with EBITDA ~11% heading to +2-4% over 18-24 months; pipes ~15% volume growth with EBITDA 4-5%; consumer appliances aiming ₹500cr+ in 2 years and ₹700-750cr by FY30 at 35-40% gross margin with a positive EBITDA swing as legacy costs clear. Bathware net bank debt fell to ₹192cr (from ₹277cr) and pipes to ₹420cr; brass prices up ~58% YoY is a cost risk. The guidance and margin roadmap are useful context given LTM sales of ₹2,604cr.
filings.impactWhy: Routine management targets and business-segment guidance.

filings.headline: Q2FY27 revenue up 30.5% to ₹496.3cr, PAT up 43% to ₹42.4cr
filings.summary: Innova Captab reported Q2FY27 revenue from operations of ₹496.3cr (up 30.5% YoY) and EBITDA of ₹72.4cr (up 29.2%), with PAT at ₹42.4cr (up 43.0%). H1FY27 revenue was ₹967.2cr (up 32.1%) with PAT of ₹86.5cr. EBITDA margin held near 14.6% while CDMO and Branded Generics momentum and the Jammu ramp-up drove strong growth against ₹1749cr trailing sales.
filings.impactWhy: Quarterly financial results; not a record volume or outlier.

filings.headline: Enters C&I energy storage; ₹2,795cr debt guarantee, ₹1,100cr CRM relocation
filings.summary: Board approved entry into a new line of business (Commercial & Industrial energy storage via WOS GNEPL), with ₹135cr capex for a 3 GWh BESS, additional ₹110cr equity (total GPIL investment in GNEPL now ₹810cr), plus ₹100cr container line, ₹100cr EV dumpers and a 26% ₹26cr stake in Solarcraft. It also approved raising ₹2,795cr debt in GNEPL (₹700cr term + ₹2,095cr working capital) backed by a corporate guarantee from GPIL, and relocated/revised the Cold Rolling Mill project to ₹1,100cr. The debt and guarantee are large against ₹5,807cr yearly sales, and the new energy-storage line marks a strategic shift beyond steel and power.
filings.impactWhy: Internal capex relocation, subsidiary guarantee, and new business entry.

filings.headline: Board approves extra ₹31cr capex, adding 3,250 tons; total expansion ₹151cr for 11,750 tons
filings.summary: Steelcast's Board approved a further ₹31cr investment in its Greenfield Foundry to add 3,250 tons capacity, on top of the earlier ₹120cr/8,500-ton plan, taking total capacity from 29,000 to 40,750 tons (up ~40%) via ₹151cr of internal accruals by FY28. Current utilisation is ~60%, expected to reach 90% by FY29, signalling strong demand. Total investment of ₹151cr is large against yearly sales of ₹441cr. The Board also declared a second interim dividend of ₹0.45/share (record date 20.11.2026).
filings.impactWhy: Incremental capacity expansion capex funded over several years.

filings.headline: Board approves extra ₹31cr for 3,250T foundry capacity, total addition 11,750T
filings.summary: Steelcast's board approved a further ₹31cr investment in its greenfield foundry to add 3,250 tons of capacity, on top of the 8,500 tons (₹120cr) approved on 29.07.2026, taking total capacity from 29,000 to 40,750 tons and total new investment to ₹151cr (≈34% of ₹441cr yearly sales), funded by internal accruals by 31/03/2028. Current utilisation is ~60%, expected to reach 90% by 31/03/2029, with expansion aimed at rising customer demand. The board also declared a second interim dividend of ₹0.45/share (record date 20.11.2026) and reported H1FY27 net profit of ₹47.4cr on sales of ₹262.8cr.
filings.impactWhy: Incremental capex announcement across multiple financial years.

filings.headline: CEO Sanjeev Agarwal resigns; Saibaba Vutukuri appointed MD (Wind Business)
filings.summary: The board noted the resignation of CEO Shri Sanjeev Agarwal with effect from close of business on 13 Nov 2026 (he stays as Advisor until 31 Dec 2026), and approved the appointment of Shri Saibaba Vutukuri as Managing Director (Wind Business) of the INOXGFL Group from 14 Nov 2026. A top-executive change at CEO/MD level is material for governance and continuity. The board also approved Q2/H1 FY27 results (Q2 standalone revenue ₹1,18,985 lakh) and granted 1,45,006 ESOPs (not material).
filings.impactWhy: Resignation of CEO and appointment of new Managing Director.

filings.headline: Nitesh Raj named CEO, Amit Bali named CFO effective 13 Nov 2026
filings.summary: The board appointed Mr. Nitesh Raj (earlier Business Head – Consumer Business) as CEO & KMP and Mr. Amit Bali (earlier Finance Controller) as CFO & KMP, both effective 13 November 2026; Mr. Kushal Jain was named Company Secretary & Compliance Officer. These are internal elevations into the top CEO and CFO roles. The board also approved unaudited Q2/H1 FY27 results: consolidated Q2 revenue ₹770.82cr (up from ₹676.31cr a year ago) with net profit after JV share of ₹6.54cr.
filings.impactWhy: Appointment of new CEO and new CFO.

filings.headline: Sold road SPVs to Indus Infra Trust; ₹578cr exceptional gain in H1
filings.summary: Along with Q2/H1 FY27 results, KNR disclosed it transferred 100% equity of several subsidiary road SPVs (KNR Palani, Guruvayur and others) to Indus Infra Trust; one tranche fetched Rs 43,248.37 lakh (~₹432cr) against Rs 14,714.31 lakh invested. These disposals produced exceptional gains of Rs 28,533.06 lakh and Rs 26,253.88 lakh, totalling Rs 57,786.93 lakh (~₹578cr) for the half year, lifting H1 net profit to ~₹563cr versus ~₹79cr a year earlier. The asset monetisation is large against yearly sales of ~₹2,673cr and reflects recycling of HAM road assets.
filings.impactWhy: Large disposal of road assets generating ₹578cr exceptional gain.

filings.headline: Relaxo to buy 51% of Kenya JV for up to ₹35.7cr, enters African market
filings.summary: Board approved a joint venture with the Kenafric Group via Relaxo Kenafric Footwears Limited (RKFL), subscribing 51% of its equity for cash of up to ₹35.70cr, making RKFL a subsidiary. The JV will manufacture, market and distribute footwear in Kenya (EVA/rubber slippers, PVC sandals, school shoes, gumboots), with asset, IP-licensing and business-transfer agreements also approved. Though the ₹35.7cr outlay is small (~1.3% of ₹2,753cr sales), it marks a strategic entry into the African market; completion expected within ~60-90 days (long-stop 6 months), subject to Kenyan and Ugandan regulatory approvals.
filings.impactWhy: JV investment outlay of ₹35.7cr is small versus sales.

filings.headline: SEBI issues show cause notice to KMPs incl CFO over insider-trading code breach
filings.summary: SEBI issued a Show Cause Notice dated Nov 6, 2026 (received Nov 12) to the company's KMPs, including CFO Pramod Gupta, his relative Ruchika Gupta, and the current and former Company Secretaries, over alleged PIT Code of Conduct violations (Clause 10 Schedule B, Regs 9(1), 3(5), 9(3)) for June–Aug 2024, tied to a July 24, 2024 corporate announcement. The company says no financial impact is expected and the noticees are evaluating their response. A SEBI insider-trading SCN against the CFO is a governance/regulatory risk worth monitoring.
filings.impactWhy: Show-cause notice received; no final order or penalty determined.

filings.headline: Signs non-binding MoU for ₹500cr API plant in Andhra Pradesh
filings.summary: Blue Jet signed a non-binding MoU with Andhra Pradesh's APEDB on 13 Nov 2026 to evaluate acquiring 50 acres and investing ₹500cr (phase-wise) for a new API manufacturing facility. The ₹500cr outlay is large versus ₹1096cr yearly sales (~46%), signalling a major capacity expansion. The MoU is valid 12 months and subject to approvals and board clearance, so execution is not yet committed.
filings.impactWhy: Non-binding MoU; investment is not yet finalized.

filings.headline: SEBI approves SG Finserve's Category III AIF registration via WoS
filings.summary: SEBI emailed approval (Nov 13, 2026) for registration of SG Finserve Multistrategy Investment Trust as a Category III Alternative Investment Fund, created by SG Alternative Investment Fund Limited, a wholly owned subsidiary. The registration number and certificate will follow on payment of the fee (within 15 days). This marks entry into a new fund-management business line, though financial impact is not yet quantified.
filings.impactWhy: Regulatory approval to register subsidiary AIF trust.

filings.headline: ICRA upgrades E2E to [ICRA] A (Positive) from A- (Stable)
filings.summary: ICRA upgraded E2E Networks' Rs 1,000 crore bank facilities to [ICRA] A (Positive) from [ICRA] A- (Stable), revising the outlook to Positive. The upgrade reflects strong revenue growth (Rs 380 crore in H1 FY2027, up 375% YoY), operating margins rising to 75%, a Rs 1,000-crore Sovereign AI contract valid to June 2029, and GPU capacity expansion. A rating upgrade signals improving credit quality and cheaper funding access for its capital-intensive growth.
filings.impactWhy: Credit rating upgraded to [ICRA] A from A-.

filings.headline: CFO RM Subramanian resigns; Suresh Narayan appointed CFO effective 13 Nov 2026
filings.summary: RM Subramanian resigned as CFO on 12 November 2026, and the board appointed Suresh Narayan as new CFO effective 13 November 2026. Narayan has been with the organisation since 2006, was part of the 2023 IPO core team, and holds an MBA. A CFO change is a KMP-level transition that investors should note.
filings.impactWhy: Resignation and appointment of Chief Financial Officer.

filings.headline: Board OKs ₹420cr JV for 2.4GW solar cell plant; Q2 PAT falls 55% to ₹4.2cr
filings.summary: Board approved a 50:50 JV with Rays Power Infra for a 2.4 GW solar cell facility at Narmadapuram (total cost ~₹1,000cr, Solarworld commitment up to ₹420cr, output by June 2027) — a large backward-integration step vs ₹973cr market cap. Q2 FY27 total income rose 81% YoY to ₹254.9cr, but EBITDA fell 16% to ₹15.2cr and PAT dropped 55% to ₹4.2cr, with EBITDA margin down 690bps to 5.9%. Also commissioned a 50 MW Assam project, got charging permission for the 200 MW Khavda project, and is exploring Data Centre EPC.
filings.impactWhy: JV investment announcement alongside regular quarterly financial results.

filings.headline: Parwada (Visakhapatnam) plant resumes full operations after temporary stoppage
filings.summary: Vishnu Chemicals' Parwada plant in Visakhapatnam, which was temporarily shut since October 28, 2026 for synchronization of forward integration and new capital projects, has resumed full operations effective today. The restart removes a production disruption and brings new integrated capacity online, supporting output against ₹1,724cr yearly sales.
filings.impactWhy: Restart of plant operations after brief scheduled temporary stoppage.

filings.headline: Non-binding MoU for 5 GWh battery giga factory, ~₹2,000cr planned in Andhra
filings.summary: Archean signed a non-binding MoU with the Andhra Pradesh Economic Development Board to explore a Battery Energy Storage Giga Factory at Visakhapatnam, with up to 5 GWh capacity and an indicative ~₹2,000cr investment via a proposed SPV. This marks a move into a new energy-storage business line, building on its stake in Offgrid Energy Labs, at a scale larger than its ₹1,180cr yearly sales. The MoU is non-binding and subject to feasibility, financing, approvals, incentives and definitive agreements, so it is not yet a firm commitment.
filings.impactWhy: Non-binding MoU for proposed battery giga factory.

filings.headline: Q2 net profit ₹119cr (+50% YoY); fabric business closed at Murbad plant
filings.summary: H1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose to ₹1,718cr (from ₹1,335cr) and net profit to ₹257cr (from ₹162cr); Q2 net profit was ₹119cr vs ₹79cr a year earlier, EPS ₹50.50. From 20 July 2026 the group discontinued its fabric manufacturing at Murbad, Thane, closing the fabric business (now a discontinued operation with only ~₹30cr H1 revenue, under 2% of yearly sales). Strong core growth with a minor non-core exit.
filings.impactWhy: Closure of minor fabric business representing under 2% of revenue.

filings.headline: Q2 PAT up 151% to ₹21.6cr; EBITDA up 235%; H2 outlook raised
filings.summary: Shriram Properties reported Q2 FY27 revenue of ₹272.3cr (+19% YoY), EBITDA of ₹62.4cr (+235%) and net profit of ₹21.6cr (+151%); H1 revenue ₹543.3cr, sales ₹1,067cr (1.76 msf). It consolidated five JVs into wholly owned subsidiaries, pushing net debt to ₹761cr (net D/E 0.5x), and guided to stronger H2 handovers (~2,300 units) with ~9 msf of new projects near closure. The strong earnings recovery and raised growth outlook are positive against ₹1,249cr of yearly sales.
filings.impactWhy: Quarterly financial results and routine operational handover targets.

filings.headline: H1 FY27 revenue up 89% to ₹1,176cr; CRISIL upgraded to A-/Positive
filings.summary: Consolidated H1 FY27 revenue from operations rose 89.13% YoY to ₹1,176.50 Cr and EBITDA 48.69% to ₹183.57 Cr, though H1 PAT slipped to ₹22.25 Cr (Q2 a seasonal monsoon loss of ₹7.51 Cr). Net debt/equity improved to 0.95x from 1.48x and CRISIL upgraded the long-term rating to A-/Positive (from BBB+/Stable). Order book stands at ₹8,633.94 Cr (5.1x FY26 revenue) and FY27 guidance of 45-50% revenue growth is reiterated.
filings.impactWhy: CRISIL upgraded long-term credit rating to A- from BBB+.

filings.headline: Manish Kumar Khandelwal appointed CFO w.e.f. 13 Nov 2026
filings.summary: Maharashtra Seamless appointed Mr Manish Kumar Khandelwal as Chief Financial Officer with effect from November 13, 2026. A CFO appointment is a key managerial change, so it is material to investors.
filings.impactWhy: Appointment of Chief Financial Officer.

filings.headline: Shareholders approve variation of IPO proceeds objects & timeline
filings.summary: Postal ballot special resolution to approve variation of the objects/terms of utilization of IPO proceeds and modify the time limit for their utilization passed with 8,66,43,406 votes (99.9955% in favour, 3,898 against) on 76% of outstanding shares polled. A change in the use of IPO funds signals a reallocation of raised capital, worth tracking for how proceeds are redeployed.
filings.impactWhy: Shareholder approval for routine modification of IPO proceeds timeline.

filings.headline: Q2 revenue ₹1,191cr (+32% YoY), PAT ₹124cr vs ₹106cr; new CFO noted
filings.summary: Q2FY27 standalone revenue from operations rose to ₹1,190.5cr from ₹901.8cr a year ago (+32%), with PAT at ₹123.9cr vs ₹106.5cr; H1 PAT was roughly flat at ₹223cr (EPS ₹19.92 vs ₹19.59). The board also noted Rakesh Mishra as CFO (w.e.f. Sep 1, 2026) and C V Kavviya as Company Secretary, and reconstituted the Risk Management Committee. Strong top-line growth but margins/profit broadly flat year on year.
filings.impactWhy: Routine quarterly financial results; CFO change was previously effective.

filings.headline: Q2 FY27 revenue ₹1,936cr up 22%, PAT ₹73cr up 31%; backlog US$1.04bn up 88%
filings.summary: Black Box posted record Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue of ₹1,936cr (up 22% YoY, 13% QoQ), EBITDA of ₹175cr (up 23%) and PAT of ₹73cr (up 31%); order backlog hit a record US$1,044mn, up 88% YoY. H1 FY27 operating cash flow reached ₹115cr and EBITDA margin expanded 50bps to 9.2%. Management reaffirmed FY27 guidance of 23-27% revenue growth, 27-32% EBITDA growth and 38-50% PAT growth, with an exit backlog target of US$1.3-1.4bn.
filings.impactWhy: Quarterly earnings release with reiterated guidance.

filings.headline: H1 revenue +22% to ₹987cr but Q2 net profit -31%; margins squeezed on expansion
filings.summary: Park Medi World reported H1 FY'27 revenue of INR 9,867mn (+22% YoY) with net profit flat at INR 1,431mn; Q2 revenue rose 25% to INR 5,110mn but net profit fell 31% to INR 545mn and EBITDA margin dropped to 19.9% from 27.5%. Occupancy fell to 55.8% (from 68.5%) as 680 new beds (Rudrapur, Panchkula) ramp up, with FY'27 capacity additions targeted at 1,430 beds (~40%). Record top-line is offset by clear near-term margin and profit compression; term debt is INR 1,779mn against cash of INR 3,713mn.
filings.impactWhy: Quarterly financial results showing margin pressure during expansion.

filings.headline: Q2 revenue +38% to ₹579.77cr but H1 PAT down 24%; Saudi delayed to Apr-27
filings.summary: Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 38.40% YoY to ₹579.77cr with PAT up 11% to ₹14.87cr, but EBITDA margin fell 184bps YoY to 6.89% as raw-material costs (copper, silver, aluminium) hit 80.6% of revenue. H1 FY27 was weaker: EBITDA down 9% and PAT down 24.21% to ₹23.20cr on 25% higher sales of ₹1,077.79cr. Management guides margins to normalise from Q3/Q4 and now expects the Saudi Arabia facility to start only April 2027 due to Middle East war escalation.
filings.impactWhy: Quarterly results with operational delay in international facility.

filings.headline: Q2 PAT up 46%, ₹186cr Power Grid order marks 765kV entry
filings.summary: Alongside Q2 FY27 results (revenue ₹238.7cr +20% YoY, PAT ₹22.2cr +46%, H1 operating cash flow of +₹82.4cr vs -₹44.1cr) SPML flagged a recently secured ₹186.41cr order from Power Grid for the Bhadla-III substation, marking its entry into 765kV transmission. The order is about 19% of ₹995cr yearly sales and opens a new business line. Company maintains guidance of minimum 25% revenue growth for FY27; net worth ₹1,184.6cr.
filings.impactWhy: Order win of ₹186.4cr is ~19% of annual sales.

filings.headline: Board approves shift from NSE Emerge to Main Board of NSE & BSE
filings.summary: Along with unaudited Q2/H1 FY27 results, the Board approved migrating the company's equity shares from the NSE Emerge SME platform to the Main Board of NSE and BSE, subject to member and regulatory approvals. Main Board migration typically improves liquidity, visibility and investor access. Q2 revenue was ₹377cr (down from ₹522cr a year ago) with net profit of ₹20cr versus ₹52cr, so growth has slowed even as the listing upgrade proceeds.
filings.impactWhy: Board approval for proposed migration from SME to Main Board.

filings.headline: Q2FY27 revenue up 19.5% to ₹558cr but PAT down 23.7% on margin squeeze
filings.summary: GSP reported Q2FY27 revenue of ₹558.4cr (up 19.5% YoY) and H1FY27 revenue of ₹944.4cr (up 11.9%), but EBITDA margin fell to 13.2% from 19.9% and PAT dropped 23.7% YoY to ₹44.6cr on raw-material cost pressure and weaker high-margin product sales. H1 PAT was ₹71cr, down 12.4%. Margins under pressure and a possible El Niño hit to rabi demand are the key risks to watch.
filings.impactWhy: Routine quarterly financial results.

filings.headline: Q2 revenue up 21% to ₹2,370cr but PAT down 74% to ₹31cr
filings.summary: Q2'FY27 revenue grew 21% YoY to ₹2,370cr, but EBITDA fell 27% to ₹255cr (margin 10.7% vs 17.8%) and reported PAT dropped 74% to ₹31cr on weak radiopharma products and Montreal remediation costs. H1 revenue ₹4,599cr (+19%) with PAT ₹87cr (-61%). The company also raised ₹800cr via NCDs for debt refinancing and capex.
filings.impactWhy: Routine quarterly financial results.

filings.headline: Relaxo to form 51% Kenya footwear JV for up to ₹35.70cr
filings.summary: Board approved a Kenya footwear manufacturing JV via Relaxo Kenafric Footwears (RKFL), subscribing 51% for cash of up to ₹35.70cr, with the Kenafric Group holding 49%. RKFL will become a subsidiary and will take over KML's Kenya footwear business plus licensed Relaxo trademarks. The outlay is small (~1.3% of ₹2753cr sales) but marks a strategic entry into the African market; subject to Kenyan and Ugandan regulatory approvals, completion in ~60-90 days (long stop 6 months).
filings.impactWhy: Small JV investment representing about 1.3% of yearly sales.

filings.headline: Q2 FY27 revenue +12.4% YoY to ₹1,000cr; PAT ₹135.7cr, EBITDA margin 20.2%
filings.summary: Usha Martin reported Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue of ₹1,000cr (up 12.4% YoY), operating EBITDA of ₹201.9cr (up 16.5%, margin 20.2%) and PAT of ₹135.7cr (up 5.9%); basic EPS ₹4.23. H1 FY27 revenue was ₹2,021.1cr and PAT ₹278cr (up 20.6%). The company holds a net cash position of ~₹415cr after ₹114cr dividends and did ₹143cr H1 capex, with elevator-rope capacity commissioning started and fully operational by Q1 FY28.
filings.impactWhy: Routine quarterly financial results.

filings.headline: H1 profit ₹257cr up 59%; fabric business shut, now a discontinued operation
filings.summary: Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue from continuing operations was ₹935.2cr (up 29% YoY from ₹725.4cr) with net profit from continuing operations of ₹117.9cr (up 49% from ₹78.9cr); H1 net profit was ₹256.8cr vs ₹161.5cr. The group discontinued its fabric manufacturing at Murbad (Thane) effective 20 July 2026, reclassifying fabric as a discontinued operation (H1 fabric revenue only ~₹30cr). Strong earnings growth plus exit from a small loss-making line; EPS (continuing) for H1 was ₹109.74.
filings.impactWhy: Discontinuation of small fabric unit contributing minimal revenue.

filings.headline: DAB awards Solarworld ₹40.3cr in SJVN EPC dispute; Q2 profit ₹12.7cr
filings.summary: Alongside unaudited Q2/H1 FY27 results, the auditor's emphasis of matter notes a favourable Dispute Adjudication Board ruling awarding Rs 402.67 million (₹40.3cr, ~2.7% of yearly sales) to the company over the suspended SJVN Green Energy EPC project. Parties are discussing release of the amount, recommencement of the project and land handover, and management is confident of recovery. Standalone H1 revenue was ₹3,394cr-equivalent reported figures with quarter profit about ₹12.7cr.
filings.impactWhy: Dispute award represents only ~2.7% of annual sales.

filings.headline: Auditor flags ongoing ED/CBI PMLA case over ₹190cr iron ore fines sale
filings.summary: Alongside Q2/H1 FY27 unaudited results, the auditor's review report draws attention to Note 4(a)/(b): attachment of land parcels at Ranchi tied to prior-year iron ore fines sales of Rs. 19,037 Lakhs (~₹190cr) allegedly in breach of mining lease terms. ED and CBI proceedings under PMLA, Prevention of Corruption Act and IPC are ongoing against the company and certain personnel. Management has made no adjustment pending outcome; the amount is about 5% of ₹3,837cr yearly sales and involves active criminal proceedings.
filings.impactWhy: Auditor emphasis of matter on previously known, ongoing proceedings.

filings.headline: Q2 revenue ₹1,191cr (+32% YoY), PAT ₹124cr (+16%)
filings.summary: ZF CV Control Systems posted Q2 FY27 (quarter ended 30.09.2026) standalone revenue from operations of ₹1,19,053.95 lakh (₹1,191cr), up ~32% from ₹90,179 lakh a year ago, with PAT of ₹12,388.91 lakh (₹124cr) vs ₹10,647 lakh, EPS ₹10.89. Half-year PAT was broadly flat at ₹22,299 lakh vs ₹22,664 lakh. The board also noted Rakesh Mishra as CFO (w.e.f. 1 Sep 2026) and reconstituted the Risk Management Committee; results are unaudited and limited-reviewed.
filings.impactWhy: Routine quarterly results; CFO appointment was already effective earlier.

filings.headline: Q2 revenue +38% to ₹580cr but H1 PAT down 24%; Saudi project delayed to Apr 2027
filings.summary: Salzer reported Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue of ₹579.77cr (up 38.40% YoY) but EBITDA margin fell to 6.89% from 8.73% as raw-material costs (copper, silver, aluminium) rose to 80.6% of revenue; Q2 PAT was ₹14.87cr. H1 FY27 PAT fell 24.21% YoY to ₹23.20cr and H1 EBITDA dropped 9.03%. Management expects margins to normalise from Q3-Q4 and now delays the Saudi Arabia facility start to April 2027 due to Middle East escalation.
filings.impactWhy: Routine quarterly results and operational facility timeline adjustment.

filings.headline: Promoter group bought 0.20% (₹5.1cr) at about ₹261
filings.summary: Promoter and promoter group members, including Ramesh Babulal Parekh, Samir Ramesh Parekh, Saurabh Ramesh Parekh, and Gandhar Coals & Mines Private Limited, bought a 0.20% stake (1,94,368 shares) through market purchases for ₹5.1 crore at an average price of ₹261, compared to the current price of ₹264. This increased their holding from 34.8% to 35.0%.
filings.impactWhy: Promoter group purchased shares in the open market.

filings.headline: H1-FY27 revenue down 28% to ₹401.5cr; Q2 revenue off 39%, small net loss
filings.summary: Yatra reported H1-FY27 consolidated revenue of INR 4,015 Mn (down 28.4% YoY) with Adjusted EBITDA of INR 301 Mn (down 40.3%) and a net loss of INR 4 Mn. Q2-FY27 revenue fell 39.1% YoY to INR 2,136 Mn with a net loss of INR 7 Mn, driven mainly by lower MICE volumes, though gross bookings grew 11% YoY to INR 42,661 Mn and Air gross margin rose 29%. The sharp revenue decline and swing to a loss against roughly ₹985cr annual sales are a clear risk despite resilient core Air/Hotel/Corporate segments.
filings.impactWhy: Routine quarterly financial results.

filings.headline: Auditors flag SEBI/NSE queries on ₹339cr IPO-proceeds advances
filings.summary: In Q2FY27 results, auditors drew attention (Note 2B) to queries from NSE and SEBI over deposits/advances of INR 3,391.44 million (~₹339cr, about 34% of yearly sales) given from IPO proceeds till June 30, 2024. The company has responded and, based on legal opinions, says the utilisation complies with the offer document. Q2 revenue was ₹166.4cr (down from ₹203.7cr a year ago) with profit of ₹9.47cr; the unresolved regulatory scrutiny on IPO-fund use is the key risk.
filings.impactWhy: Auditor emphasis of matter, not a qualification or resignation.

filings.headline: Board approves reclassifying promoter Bhaskar Srinivasan (9.42%) to public
filings.summary: Avalon's board approved the request of promoter Mr. Bhaskar Srinivasan and his promoter-group trusts to be reclassified from 'Promoter' to 'Public' category, subject to SEBI Reg 31A approvals. The applicants hold 63,04,070 shares (9.42%), with Bhaskar Srinivasan himself at 49,34,120 (7.38%), and confirm they hold under 10% voting rights and exercise no control or board/KMP role. The move reduces the identified promoter holding, a notable governance change though no shares change hands.
filings.impactWhy: Promoter reclassification to public category with no share transaction.

filings.headline: Q2FY27 revenue ₹2,627cr up 60% YoY but adjusted loss of ₹57cr
filings.summary: Consolidated Q2FY27 revenue was ₹2,627cr (up 60% YoY) with Operating EBITDA of ₹127cr (up 30%), but the company posted an adjusted loss after tax of ₹57cr for the quarter plus an exceptional loss of ₹9.5cr (₹132.7cr for H1). H1FY27 revenue was ₹6,515cr (up 28%) with adjusted PAT of ₹69cr. Strong top-line growth led by Electronics (+94%) and Consumer Durables (+41%) but the quarterly bottom-line loss and large H1 exceptional charge are a concern.
filings.impactWhy: Routine quarterly financial results.

filings.headline: Board OKs variation in IPO objects: 6 of 19 IVF centres relocated, timeline to FY29
filings.summary: Board approved a variation in IPO object No.1 (19 new IVF centres), substituting 6 cities/locations and pushing completion to Fiscal 2029, subject to a special resolution via postal ballot; the ₹5,000 Lakh allocation is unchanged. A change in the use of IPO funds and schedule signals execution slippage on the expansion plan. The Board also approved H1 results (Q2 revenue ₹2,805.68 lakh) and appointed Dr. Ravish Manchanda as National Head – Operations, a sub-CFO/CEO role.
filings.impactWhy: Routine adjustment to IPO timeline and centre locations.

filings.headline: Board OKs ₹425cr warrants to Zollner; Q2 PAT up 60% to ₹39.8cr
filings.summary: Avalon's board approved a preferential issue of warrants worth ₹425cr to JV partner Zollner Elektronik AG, subject to shareholder approval at an EGM. At the current price of ₹2108.5 that implies roughly 0.20cr new shares, about 3% more shares and ~2.9% dilution to existing holders (issue price not disclosed in the filing). Alongside, Q2 FY27 revenue rose 37.4% YoY to ₹525.4cr and PAT 59.5% to ₹39.8cr, and the company formed a strategic JV with Zollner and signed a Tamil Nadu MOU for 25 acres.
filings.impactWhy: Warrant issue dilution is below the 5% threshold.

filings.headline: Ethanol allocation of ₹1,715cr from OMCs; total supply value ₹3,382cr for ESY 2026-27
filings.summary: TruAlt Bioenergy was allocated 2,74,832 KL (27.48 crore litres) of ethanol worth ₹1,715.27 crore for ESY 2026-27 supply to BPCL, HPCL, IOCL and MRPL. Including Nayara Energy supply, carried-forward supplies, DDGS/DWGS by-products and ENA sales, the aggregate value is about ₹3,382.29 crore. This is roughly 123% of annual sales (₹2,747cr), a very large order secured for the year running 01.11.2026 to 31.10.2027.
filings.impactWhy: Order allocation represents over 60% of annual sales.

filings.headline: Brace Port H1 revenue up 35% to ₹44.4cr; targets doubling revenue in FY28
filings.summary: Material subsidiary Brace Port Logistics reported H1 FY27 consolidated revenue of ₹44.43cr (up 34.9% YoY) and PAT of ₹3.47cr (up 39.5%), and guided to doubling revenue in FY28 plus plans for ₹7.5cr warehousing/3PL-4PL investment and a 76% SageRoute stake. Separately, Skyways invested ₹42.42cr for 16,96,791 shares at ₹250 each in subsidiary Forin Container Line (now 85.84% held) to cut its debt, a related-party rights allotment. The growth outlook and subsidiary expansion are positive for the holding company's value.
filings.impactWhy: Subsidiary financial results and internal operational targets.

filings.headline: Q2 revenue +17.9% to ₹37.4cr but H1 PAT -10.5%; margins squeezed by new hubs
filings.summary: Q2 FY27 revenue rose 17.9% YoY to ₹37.4cr but EBITDA fell 2.1% to ₹13.5cr (margin 36.0%, down 737bps) and PAT was flat at ₹9.4cr. H1 FY27 PAT fell 10.5% to ₹11.2cr with margins compressed by rollout costs and fixed-cost drag from two new hubs (South Extension, Gurgaon) under a planned 19-centre expansion. Revenue momentum is strong but profitability is under pressure as new hubs ramp; management expects a stronger H2.
filings.impactWhy: Routine quarterly financial results.

filings.headline: Skyways invested ₹42.4cr in subsidiary Forin Container Line; holding now 85.84%
filings.summary: Skyways was allotted 16,96,791 fresh equity shares of material subsidiary Forin Container Line at ₹250 each (₹240 premium), aggregating ₹42.42cr, via a rights issue to help the subsidiary repay debt; its stake rises to 85.84%. The deal is a related-party transaction done at arm's length, funded from IPO proceeds. No new Skyways shares are issued, so there is no dilution to existing shareholders; separately the filing notes subsidiary Brace Port's H1 FY27 revenue up 34.9% to ₹44.43cr and PAT up 39.5% to ₹3.47cr.
filings.impactWhy: Internal capital infusion into existing subsidiary.

filings.headline: Madras HC ruling cuts tax contingent liability by ₹106cr
filings.summary: Mahindra Holidays received a favourable Madras High Court order on 12 Nov 2026 upholding its revenue-deferral accounting method for AY 2006-07 and 2007-08. The ruling reduces the company's contingent liability by ₹106cr, about 3.4% of ₹3,090cr yearly sales. The outcome removes a long-pending tax overhang in the company's favour.
filings.impactWhy: Favourable court ruling on contingent liability under 5% of sales.

filings.headline: Richa Jain elevated from Deputy CFO to CFO effective Nov 12, 2026
filings.summary: Ceinsys Tech's Board promoted CA Richa Jain from Deputy CFO to Chief Financial Officer with effect from November 12, 2026, a KMP-level appointment. The Board also gave in-principle approval to set up a wholly owned subsidiary in the UAE and appointed Mr. Bala Pavan Kumar Tsunduru as President from December 7, 2026. Unaudited Q2/H1 FY27 results were also approved.
filings.impactWhy: Appointment of Chief Financial Officer.

filings.headline: Q2 FY27 revenue up 19.4% YoY to ₹277.9cr; distillery revenue up 30.5%
filings.summary: Piccadily Agro reported Q2 FY27 Revenue from Operations of ₹277.9cr, up 19.4% YoY from ₹232.7cr, with distillery revenue up 30.5% to ₹271.3cr (97.6% of revenue vs 89.3% a year ago). EBITDA rose 9.6% YoY to ₹53cr and H1 FY27 PAT was higher than last year. Maturation capacity reached 96,000 barrels against a revised FY target of over 1,00,000 barrels, underscoring continued momentum in the premium spirits portfolio.
filings.impactWhy: Routine quarterly financial results.

filings.headline: Deep Saraf named MD; Q2FY27 PAT up 51.8% to ₹808Mn, revenue up 41.9%
filings.summary: Manorama announced a leadership transition: Deep Saraf becomes Managing Director (operations/execution), Mudit Kumar Singh as Chairman, with Ashish Saraf moving to President–Strategic Planning.
